case: declaring a real, non-admitted primitive in the not-admitted block
why: The benign twin of r19-not-admitted-operator-is-also-admitted. `present` is a registered primitive, its only argument is a VALUE position, and it is not in ADMISSIBLE_LITERAL -- so naming it in `#/admissible_ancestors_not_admitted` states something true, adds a row a future author can read, and contradicts nothing. This must PASS. The block is meant to grow: every operator that takes the `quantified` escape is REQUIRED to be named here, so a checker that refused a new row would refuse the declaration the escape now costs. It also exercises the block's second rule in the passing direction -- the name is a primitive that exists, which is what separates this from a row forbidding an operator no body could carry.

patch.value: `present(value: X)` type-checks X and asserts nothing about it, so its one argument is a value position and no conjunct inside it is demanded (RC3-02). Never admissible as an ancestor of a pinned conjunct.
